## FX Index Dashboard – End of Round 4

The FX Index tracks how each currency is performing in the market **without requiring students to do any calculations**.

::: {.callout-note}
**How to read this table:** Higher scores indicate strengthening / inflows. Lower scores indicate depreciation pressure / outflows.
:::

| Country | FX Index | Status | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Atlantica | 101.4 | Stable | Credibility remains strong, though markets now read policy partly through a growth lens. |
| Noravia | 101.0 | Stable | Tight policy still supports the currency, but slower growth is becoming a concern. |
| Pacifica | 101.2 | Stable | Trade links and earlier support continue to support stability. |
| Industralia | 100.8 | Stable / softening | Industrial and trade exposure leave it more vulnerable to slower external demand. |
| Mercatoria | 100.7 | Stable / softening | Trade diplomacy helps, but export dependence matters more in a weaker global environment. |
| Petrovia | 100.4 | Softening | Commodity-linked economies are beginning to feel the effects of weaker demand. |
| Agrona | 99.7 | Softening | Fiscal discipline remains credible, but commodity sensitivity is creating renewed market pressure. |
| Frontieria | 100.2 | Stable | Restricted capital and cautious policy continue to limit volatility. |

::: {.callout-important}
**Reminder:** The FX Index is a summary indicator. A stable currency does not necessarily mean a strong economy.
:::

## Trade & Alliance Tracker – End of Round 4

Trade diplomacy remains active, but the market is now evaluating agreements through the lens of the **developing global slowdown**.

::: {.callout-note}
**Interpretation:** Agreements now matter not only for currency stability, but also for whether countries can preserve trade flows and soften the impact of weaker global demand.
:::

## Active Trade Relationships

| Agreement / Relationship | Type | Countries | Current Market View |
|---|---|---|---|
| Atlantica–Pacifica–Noravia Link | Bilateral / overlapping outreach | Atlantica, Pacifica, Noravia | Helpful for market access and credibility, but still developing |
| Industralia–Mercatoria–Noravia Framework | Multilateral / Open | Industralia, Mercatoria, Noravia | Potentially important if global demand weakens further |
| Petrovia–Agrona Strategic Link | Strategic Goods | Petrovia, Agrona | More valuable now because commodity earnings are under pressure |

## Market Interpretation

- Broader, more credible trade frameworks are becoming more valuable as global growth slows.
- Strategic-goods agreements may help protect export earnings and supply access.
- Countries without meaningful trade ties risk relative isolation if demand weakens further.

## Countries Most Likely to Benefit from Deeper Trade Integration

| Country | Why Trade Matters More Now |
|---|---|
| Industralia | Industrial exporters need demand support if external growth softens |
| Mercatoria | Trade-oriented economies benefit from preserving market access |
| Agrona | Commodity-sensitive economies need stronger external demand anchors |
| Petrovia | Strategic resource ties can soften the effects of weaker commodity demand |

## Economic Conditions Index – End of Round 4

The **Economic Conditions Index** is a simple indicator of each country's current growth environment.

- **100** = baseline / normal conditions
- **Above 100** = stronger-than-baseline growth conditions
- **Below 100** = slowing growth or weaker demand conditions

::: {.callout-note}
This index is separate from the FX Index. A country can have a stable currency while its economy is slowing.
:::

| Country | Economic Conditions Index | Current Economic Status | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Atlantica | 98.8 | Slowing modestly | Still resilient, but tighter global conditions are weighing on growth. |
| Noravia | 97.9 | Slowing | Tight policy and weaker external demand are beginning to constrain activity. |
| Pacifica | 98.6 | Slowing modestly | Stable externally, but trade sensitivity remains important. |
| Industralia | 98.4 | Slowing | Industrial and trade dependence are beginning to matter more. |
| Mercatoria | 98.5 | Slowing | Export-oriented structure leaves it exposed to softer demand. |
| Petrovia | 97.8 | Slowing | Weaker global demand is softening the outlook for resource-linked economies. |
| Agrona | 97.4 | Slowing more sharply | Commodity sensitivity makes Agrona especially vulnerable to a slowdown. |
| Frontieria | 98.9 | Near flat / weak growth | Policy caution supports stability, but growth remains subdued. |

::: {.callout-important}
The system is now showing a **developing global slowdown**: currencies remain relatively stable, but economic activity is beginning to soften.
:::
